fields.description_1: The information found on the website was quite helpful for language-related queries. However, the tone used was very high-sounding and prioritization was not very clear in the text. The readers should be given a clear picture about the website and what they can get out of it just by having a glance.
fields.description_2: In the end, there is a better website that does not just inform others about what your language service can do for you, but also gives answers that would be easy for any visitor to understand. I have organized the text in such a way that it provides answers to the questions asked by the visitor.

fields.description_1: There was need for QuickTemp to provide answers to practical questions raised by their site visitors much faster. The job offer must be clearly explained with relevant details, context, and a way of contacting them. If not, the site might lose its focus hence appearing generic; it made quick judgment possible before any contact.
fields.description_2: This is how I improved the page by getting rid of redundant parts, arranging the info properly, and making each block more scannable. This WordPress version of the recruiting pitch delivers all the information in a realistic setting, allowing people to see why it makes sense to keep on reading.

fields.description_1: There were many reasons why a clearer website was needed by VC Het Wonder for their health care project. Visitors had to be able to read the message and make their contact very quickly. The story that was there already lacked structure and clear wording. There was need for better and easy scanning information when writing about a health care organization.
fields.description_2: My method of approaching Vchetwonder involved the use of a cleaner design through the application of WordPress and microcopy to make VC Het Wonder have more of a particular feel that can be easily navigated by those who are interested in viewing the projects.

fields.description_1: Internal links can become unorganized when there is a manual process of creating the links. This is because there will be difficulty in knowing which page should be linked, what content is not being properly linked and other similar issues.
fields.description_2: The Super Simple Internal Links makes it easy for users to control internal linking on WordPress sites. This tool will assist in organizing links to other pages or posts, provide proper structuring for websites, and make navigation easier while avoiding manual management of all the links.

fields.description_1: However, prior to this change, the Starkeuken web pages required more focused information regarding the kitchen specifics as they were not apparent at first sight for some visitors. In addition, the site had to have an appealing opening statement, proper navigation and simple wording describing the deal before they contacted the company.
fields.description_2: I refined the site by giving it more structure, cleaner English writing, and a more cohesive path through the introduction and contact form. This page provides a clean and concise overview of the kitchen services, making it easier for visitors to make comparisons and maintaining consistency throughout the WordPress layout on any device size.

fields.description_1: AC Drive needed a website that helps new learners choose a driving school with confidence. Visitors had to understand the lesson options, packages, instructors, pricing and service areas without feeling overwhelmed. The page also needed to answer common questions early, build trust and make the first inquiry feel easy.
fields.description_2: The website was structured around clear lesson information, trust signals, package options and quick contact routes. Short sections explain what learners can expect before booking. Call, WhatsApp and trial lesson buttons stay easy to reach on mobile, helping visitors move from comparing driving schools to contacting AC Drive.

fields.description_1: Images can appear in many places across a WordPress website, which makes it difficult to see where each file is being used. Website owners also need to know whether an image is still active before replacing, removing or optimising it.
fields.description_2: Image Usage Scanner helps WordPress users find where images are used across their website. The tool gives website owners a clearer overview of media usage, making it easier to manage files, clean up the media library and avoid removing images that are still needed.

fields.description_1: When course dates are spread across different pages or files, it becomes difficult for visitors to see which dates are available. It also makes the content harder for website administrators to maintain, especially when schedules change often.
fields.description_2: Course Dates Manager gives WordPress users a dedicated way to manage and display course dates. Upcoming sessions can be organised in one clear schedule, making the information easier to update for administrators and easier to understand for visitors before they register.

fields.description_1: Making changes to WordPress code can be risky when updates are handled through loose snippets. Instructions have to be copied, pasted, and placed in the right files, which increases the chance of mistakes. This becomes even more fragile when a patch affects several parts of the codebase.
fields.description_2: I created a plugin that turns patching into a structured process inside WordPress. JSON instructions are displayed clearly, validated, and prepared for review before deployment. Developers stay in control, making fixes easier to inspect, test, adjust, and apply without relying on messy manual steps.

fields.description_1: Managing ACF fields across larger WordPress websites can quickly become difficult. Texts, descriptions, alt texts, and field values are often spread across many screens. That makes content slower to check, harder to update, and more vulnerable to mistakes when editing, exporting, or restoring data.
fields.description_2: I designed a WordPress plugin that exports ACF data, structures it for editing, and imports updated content back into the website. The admin interface groups fields by item and keeps the current values visible. This gives teams a cleaner workflow for reviewing, updating, and restoring content without opening every page separately.

fields.description_1: WordPress sites have the ability to accumulate large amounts of images very rapidly, leading to difficulties in maintaining an overview of all the images in use. This may cause users to overlook the availability of images, the places where they are used, or other pending tasks.
fields.description_2: ModernImage provides an organized view of images for the user. It enables the user to locate his or her WordPress images easily. It provides better management of images. Users can control images through this plug-in effectively.

fields.description_1: Managing ACF content manually can quickly become inefficient and disorganized. Administrators often have to open each page separately to update text, SEO fields, and image information. On larger websites, this creates duplication, reduces visibility, and makes it harder to keep content consistent.
fields.description_2: This plugin helps WordPress users manage internal page content from one central place. It saves time, reduces repetitive work, and removes the need for extra third-party tools in many cases. The workflow becomes simpler, clearer, and easier to maintain for daily content updates.

fields.description_1: Spring Architecten needed a website that could present a broad and varied portfolio in a clearer way. With projects across education, housing, healthcare, heritage, transformations, and new construction, the website had to stay organized without feeling overwhelming. The main challenge was to combine the studio’s human-centered vision, sustainable approach, and inspiring project work into one clear and user-friendly experience.
fields.description_2: I created a more direct website structure with clearer navigation, calm page layouts, and a stronger focus on project presentation. Visitors can browse through the portfolio more easily and quickly understand the studio’s expertise. The design gives enough space to visuals, short descriptions, and key project details, creating a professional presentation that reflects the identity of an architecture studio focused on people, space, light, and sustainable buildings.

fields.description_1: Finding suitable licensed images for SEO pages often slows down production when search, approval, downloading and ACF placement happen manually across separate tools, creating extra checks, duplicated work and avoidable delays before content can be published confidently at scale online.
fields.description_2: SEO Image Assistant connects Shutterstock search, review queues, licensing, downloads and ACF field mapping inside WordPress, making image selection clearer, easier and safer to manage while reducing manual steps and keeping approved assets aligned with SEO page requirements at scale.

fields.description_1:
Hotels often need extra cleaning and housekeeping staff at short notice, but visitors only take action when the offer, reliability and next step are immediately clear. The previous presentation did not show strongly enough which roles DCA can provide, how quickly hotels can scale and why clients can trust the quality.

Important SEO content around hotel staff, housekeeping, room attendants and cleaners was too scattered, while those search terms are commercially valuable for new hotel enquiries.
fields.description_2:
I structured the page around one clear search intent: quickly requesting reliable hotel staff. The hero immediately communicates the main benefits, followed by role-specific sections for cleaners, housekeeping staff, room attendants and assistants.

Reviews, certificates and recruiter photos build trust, while blog cards create extra SEO entry points. Short copy, clear calls to action and local contact details create a human, conversion-focused landing page that supports both search engines and hotel managers looking for flexible staff.

fields.description_1: Babylon Safety needed a website that could present urgent fire safety services clearly without overwhelming visitors. The offer covers emergency fire guards, event safety, inspections, training and regional deployment, so the page had to guide different audiences quickly. The existing communication risked feeling too broad, making it harder for companies, venues and organizers to understand when to call, which service fits their situation and why Babylon Safety is a reliable partner during high-pressure safety decisions.
fields.description_2: I structured the website around speed, trust and service clarity. A strong hero communicates immediate availability, followed by recognizable client logos, service cards, statistics, regional coverage and practical benefits. Visual sections with firefighters, training scenes and emergency contexts make the offer feel concrete. Clear calls to action guide visitors toward requesting support, while supporting content for vacancies, safety services and locations strengthens SEO and helps Babylon Safety reach both urgent buyers and long-term partners online.

fields.description_1: Managing multilingual WordPress content can quickly become fragmented. Languages, translated strings, SEO details, review status, and import/export tasks often sit in different places, making it harder to keep content consistent and ready for publication.
fields.description_2: This WordPress translate plugin  brings the translation workflow into one structured WordPress admin experience. It helps you configure languages, scan content, review translation status, manage CSV imports and exports, and display a clean frontend language switcher for visitors.

fields.description_1:
Managing stock images for SEO pages can be slow and repetitive. Editors often need to search externally, license images, download files, upload them to WordPress and manually connect them to the right page fields.

This creates extra admin work and increases the chance of inconsistent filenames, missing image data or duplicated media usage across larger websites.
fields.description_2:
I worked on a custom WordPress plugin that connects WordPress with the Shutterstock API. The plugin lets users search for images, license selected assets, import them into the media library and attach them to structured page fields.

The work focused on making the plugin safer and more production-ready, including stronger media validation, safer licensing recovery, improved OAuth handling and better performance for larger media libraries.

fields.description_1:
DCA Dienstverlening offered a wide range of cleaning and facility services, but the previous website did not clearly communicate the full scope of its expertise. Visitors had difficulty identifying the right service for their needs, and the path from landing on the website to requesting a quote lacked clarity.

Valuable trust signals such as customer reviews, client logos, and completed projects were also not integrated effectively throughout the user journey. In addition, the site's SEO structure did not fully support visibility for high-intent local and service-related search terms.
fields.description_2:
I designed and developed a conversion-focused WordPress website that prioritizes clarity, trust, and lead generation. The homepage was structured around a clear value proposition supported by Google Reviews, client references, and service highlights. Individual service pages were organized into an SEO-friendly architecture targeting relevant commercial search queries.

Strategic calls-to-action, quote request forms, and contact options were placed throughout the website to reduce friction and encourage enquiries. The entire website was built responsively to deliver a consistent experience across desktop, tablet, and mobile devices.

fields.description_1: Managing image fields across WordPress content can be repetitive and error-prone, especially on sites using Advanced Custom Fields. Editors often need to manually open posts, pages, products or terms, select images, check existing values and avoid accidental overwrites. This slows down content workflows and increases the risk of inconsistent media usage.
fields.description_2: ACF Image Auto Filler centralizes this workflow in a dedicated WordPress admin interface. The plugin scans eligible ACF image fields, lets users select content and Media Library images, previews the mapping before changes are made, and safely fills supported fields or featured images. It includes overwrite protection, rollback per saved run, an audit log, batch mode, manual field mapping, CSV dry-run export and support for ACF group image fields.

fields.description_1: Wehear4u needed project content that was easier to read and more useful for quick comparison. The page had to explain the healthcare work in clear, accessible language, while giving visitors enough context to understand the service, trust the presentation, and decide whether to get in touch.
fields.description_2: I structured the page around what visitors need to know first: the offer, the benefit, and the next step. Short sections, clearer wording, and focused WordPress delivery make the healthcare project easier to assess. The page now feels more specific, practical, and ready for inquiries.

fields.description_1: Fidelyaa needed consultancy content that explains the offer clearly without sounding too broad. Visitors had to understand the service, the value and the reason to make contact within a short amount of time.
fields.description_2: I improved the page with a clearer introduction, more focused service sections and practical wording that supports decision-making. The WordPress layout now presents the consultancy offer in a more confident and readable way, with a contact route that feels natural.

fields.description_1:
WooCommerce stores that rely on external fulfillment workflows need more than basic order management. Orders must be sent reliably, shipping labels need to be generated safely, tracking updates must return to WooCommerce, and failed syncs need a clear recovery flow.

Without a dedicated integration, these steps often become manual, inconsistent and difficult to monitor. That increases admin work and creates avoidable risk around order processing, customer communication and shipping status updates.
fields.description_2:
I worked on a custom WooCommerce plugin that connects WooCommerce orders with the SooCool workflow. The plugin supports order syncing, label generation, tracking updates, webhook handling and admin tools for retrying failed processes.

The work focused on making the integration safer and more production-ready, including stronger webhook validation, secure label download flows, cleaner queue handling and improved compatibility with modern WooCommerce order storage.

fields.description_1: Updating pages, posts and products manually becomes inefficient when ACF fields, Yoast text, summaries, images and media details are spread across separate editing screens daily.
fields.description_2: The plugin exports structured TXT files and imports reviewed updates back into WordPress, while preserving existing content and media unless administrators choose otherwise during import.

fields.description_1: The WooCommerce Egaline Calculator needed a clearer WordPress plugin page, so visitors could understand the purpose of the tool before taking action. The existing story needed more structure, shorter explanations, and less generic wording to make the value of the plugin easier to judge.
fields.description_2: This plugin helps WordPress users manage an internal calculation process from one central place. It reduces manual work, saves time, and limits the need for extra third-party tools. The result is a more practical workflow that makes the task easier to complete and easier to maintain.
